document_title: TLC VACATIONS LLP — TBO Flight and Hotel API Test Scenarios
document_type: Test scenario specification and request for TBO staging fixtures
format_note: This JSON describes test scenarios. It is not a TBO API request/response payload or executed certification evidence. Workflow keys and shared conventions are defined in plan_context.

plan_context.section: 1. Request to the TBO integration team
paragraphs: TLC VACATIONS LLP requests an account-specific staging test pack for flight and hotel integration. Please map the scenarios below to supported API methods and provide reproducible request/response JSON, seeded inventory or trigger instructions, and the expected status transitions. Where a capability is not supported, please mark it Unsupported and provide the supported alternative.

This is a proposed test specification and response-fixture request, not an execution report or a claim of certification. Every scenario starts as Not run. It does not ask TBO to change its production API schema. No API login, booking, ticketing, cancellation or live payment is performed in preparing this document.

TLC’s client experience is: explore destinations → compare and save hotels/flights → request a tailored TLC quote → consultant review and supplier revalidation → approved fulfilment. A shortlist or quote acceptance must never be presented as a confirmed reservation. Booking scenarios below support supplier certification and controlled staff fulfilment, not instant client checkout.

Prepared 17 October 2026 • Version 1.0 • Audience: TBO integration/support team and TLC engineering/QA. Passwords, tokens and customer records are deliberately excluded. The referenced email was available; separate attachments were not available for review.

plan_context.section: 2. Confirm these items before preparing the fixtures
paragraphs: Q01 — Flight certification scope: the onboarding email specifies cases 1–7; the public Flight Certification page specifies 1–5, with later cases conditional; the Flight API Guide says 1–10. Please confirm the binding checklist/version for TLC in writing. This plan includes cases 1–12, with 1–7 treated as onboarding-required pending confirmation. [S1–S3]

Q02 — Flight paths: public sample guidance distinguishes LCC direct Ticket from non-LCC Book → Ticket. Confirm exceptions, special-return handling and NDC flow for this account. Do not require a generic Book call on every LCC itinerary. [S1]

Q03 — Hotel product/version: the email lists Hotel Info → Hotel Room → Hotel Block, while the current hotel documentation exposes Search → PreBook → Book with BookingCode. Confirm TLC’s entitled family, staging base URLs, authentication for each service and the exact method mapping. Do not mix identifiers or payloads between families. The hotel guide URL in the email appears malformed; this plan references the guide linked from the documentation navigation. [S4–S7]

Q04 — Hotel access: a prior TLC project verification record dated 6 October 2026 reports successful static-content and flight authentication but hotel availability rejecting access credentials. This is historical evidence, not a new test result. Please confirm Hotel Search/PreBook/Book entitlement and whether separate hotel credentials are required.

Q05 — Test setup: provide permitted egress IPs, ClientId, API versions, airline/source enablement, test wallet/credit, bookable dates and synthetic traveller details. Specify safe staging issue/cancel/refund rules and how to clean up test reservations.

Q06 — Sessions and retry rules: confirm token/session lifetime, trace and booking-code expiry, retryable error codes, polling intervals, request-reference deduplication, timeout reconciliation and duplicate prevention across all booking methods.

Q07 — Static data: supply current city IDs and hotel codes, de-duplication mappings, incremental/full-refresh guidance, retirement handling and update cadence. Please identify which content/rates can be retained and for how long.

Q08 — Financial semantics: confirm currency, rounding, per-passenger/per-room/whole-booking totals, agent net versus selling amounts, minimum selling restrictions, taxes, supplements, commission and refund settlement fields. These are API data-contract questions, not proposed tax calculations.

Q09 — Evidence and support: confirm the staging support recipient, because the supplied email’s visible address and mailto target differ. Confirm a secure channel for raw certification logs and whether correlation IDs must remain unredacted. Never include API passwords or access tokens in the general test-plan pack.

Q10 — Data/AI rights: confirm contractual rights for storage, client display, caching, embeddings and model training on supplier content, including images. TLC will keep changing prices and availability live-grounded; a trained model will not be the authority for booking facts. These permissions are not assumed.

Q11 — Please return supported/unsupported status, owner and target delivery date for each case. For negative cases that cannot be seeded in staging, provide an explicitly labelled mock fixture and the production error contract; such fixtures do not constitute certification evidence.

D = actual execution date in the agreed test timezone. Standard departure/check-in = D+30; return/check-out = D+35. Recalculate dates each run; TBO may nominate other available dates. Boundary cases deliberately vary those dates. Store timestamps with timezone and UTC equivalent.

Adult/child/infant counts are shown as A/C/I. Default test ages on travel date: adults 34 and 32; children 6 and 10 (single child 8); infant 1. Generate synthetic DOBs to match those ages and exercise return-date birthdays separately. TBO must confirm airline and hotel age-band rules; hotel child occupancy is not assumed to equal airline child/infant classification.

Domestic candidates: DEL–BOM flights and New Delhi hotels. International candidates: DEL–DXB flights and Dubai hotels. These are requested fixtures, not guaranteed staging inventory. TBO should return accepted airport codes, new city IDs, hotel codes, nationalities and replacement routes if necessary. Default nationality is IN; nationality variants are specified explicitly.

Use TBO-approved synthetic names, contacts, passports and tax identifiers, with exactly the required lead traveller designation and complete required fields. No real customer data is needed. Do not invent realistic document numbers and send them to suppliers.

P0 = certification baseline, reservation correctness, money or recovery blocker. P1 = required functional/regression coverage before the applicable feature launches. P2 = optional capability, enabled only when agreed. Priority is TLC’s risk classification; it is not TBO’s mandatory-case numbering.

Execution modes: STAGING = TBO-backed controlled integration run; MOCK = explicitly synthetic contract/fault fixture; LOCAL = TLC application test. Negative/high-volume cases require TBO-approved seeds or local fault injection, not uncontrolled requests against a supplier. Record the mode for every result.

Common evidence E: case ID, run ID, prerequisite fixture version, environment, execution time, API version/method, redacted request/response JSON, HTTP status/headers, latency, correlation identifiers, final supplier state, TLC assertion and operator. Complete booking cases include retrieval evidence; failed pre-booking cases stop at the expected error and must not manufacture a booking ID.

plan_context.section: 4. Workflow keys used in the scenario tables
paragraphs: G — Non-LCC/GDS: Authenticate → Search → FareRule → FareQuote → SSR when selected/supported → Book → Ticket → GetBookingDetails. L — LCC: Authenticate → Search → FareRule → FareQuote → SSR when selected/supported → Ticket → GetBookingDetails. Apply the selected result’s provider-confirmed flow. [S1]

R — Return execution: standard domestic returns may require separate outbound and inbound chains; international returns and special returns can have different grouping. TBO must supply the applicable result-index transition and PNR structure. Carry forward current response identifiers rather than creating or reusing unrelated ones. [S3]
N — NDC: run only after TBO provides the enabled airline, request schema, booking/ticket path and ancillary restrictions. Do not assume NDC is interchangeable with a GDS or LCC payload.

H — Hotel: use current static IDs/content, Authenticate/Authorize as required by the agreed endpoint family, Search, details enrichment, PreBook (or the family’s Room/Block operations), Book and GetBookingDetails. Confirm voucher and cancellation steps separately. The published current guide uses BookingCode, with session/trace diagnostics. [S5–S7]

For all successful baseline cases: check selected itinerary/room and party consistency, valid price/currency, correct traveller mapping, required rules, final identifiers and status, and reconciliation in booking retrieval. For repricing or policy changes, require explicit TLC review before committing. Never retry an uncertain Book/Ticket blindly.

plan_context.section: 5. Response pack requested for every scenario
paragraphs: For each scenario ID, return: Supported / Conditional / Unsupported; actual API product/version; method sequence; reproducible setup; valid synthetic input; raw request and response for each applicable step; HTTP and application-level outcomes; field definitions; final state; and recovery guidance. Use the attached CSV as the response tracker.

Provide real staging logs for successful certification chains. For deterministic negative cases, identify the seed or switch that reproduces the state. If only a mock is available, label every file MOCK and explain which production behaviour it models. Do not substitute fabricated successful PNRs or confirmations for certification evidence.

For any list/array, clarify indexing, ordering, nullability and cardinality. For money, identify currency, decimal precision, rounding, unit and whether tax/fees are included. For dates, identify timezone and inclusive/exclusive boundaries. For status/error fields, provide actual enum/code values; this document does not invent them.

For booking timeouts and duplicate attempts, include both committed and not-committed outcomes, approved lookup identifiers, retry rules and financial effects. Include eventual-consistency windows and escalation instructions where a state cannot be resolved automatically.

Flight response coverage requested: carrier/source, segments, cabin/fare brand, result linkage, passenger-type fare breakdown, rule and baggage evidence, SSR eligibility/prices, booking/ticket identifiers and retrieval states. Hotel coverage requested: static identity, bookable room combination, occupancy mapping, price/currency, inclusions, policy/charge scope, required guest fields, reservation/voucher IDs and retrieval states. Unsupported fields must be identified, not filled with invented values.

Use one folder per case and one request/response pair per method: TLC_TBO_STAGING/<case-id>/<run-id>/manifest.json; 01-authenticate.request.json; 01-authenticate.response.json; 02-search.request.json; 02-search.response.json; …; final-booking-details.response.json; assertions.json. For a negative case, the final file is the expected error or reconciliation response, not a fabricated booking.

The manifest is TLC’s test metadata, not a TBO API payload. Record caseId, runId, mode, environment, apiFamily, apiVersion, executedAtWithOffset, executedAtUtc, fixtureVersion, step filenames, request/session/trace identifiers as permitted, supplier reference if present, outcome and defect reference. Keep credentials in environment variables outside this pack.

Each assertion record states expected versus actual, evidence file/JSON path, result (Pass / Fail / Blocked / Not applicable) and reviewer. Mark Not applicable only with a reason and TBO agreement for certification items. A passed mock test is not a passed staging certification case.

Redact passwords, authentication headers, access tokens, payment secrets and unnecessary personal data. Preserve correlation IDs in the restricted support bundle when required by TBO; use stable aliases in wider copies. Agree any exceptions through a secure transfer channel rather than weakening general application log redaction.
Phase 1 — TBO confirms Q01–Q11, API families, access, current static IDs and test fixtures. Resolve hotel entitlement before interpreting availability failures as product behaviour.

Phase 2 — Execute AIR-SAMPLE and obtain sample approval. Prepare the flight crosswalk cases required by TBO’s written account-specific checklist and all eight listed hotel occupancy cases. Submit each completed case separately with JSON evidence and the original sample-verification reference. [S2,S4]

Phase 3 — Execute applicable P0 and P1 scenarios from sections D–H. TLC local tests cover orchestration, data access, UI, notifications and financial reconciliation; TBO supplies supplier-side fixtures and contract clarification. P2 capabilities remain disabled until scoped and verified.

Exit criteria: required certification cases accepted by TBO; no open P0 defect; applicable P1 defects resolved or explicitly accepted with owner and mitigation; uncertain reservations reconciled; no duplicate bookings/debits; required fields, fare/policy changes and cancellations handled; production configuration and monitoring reviewed. TBO must issue its own certification/sign-off.

No scenario has been executed for this document. Proposed owner split: TBO supplies valid schemas, supported inventory, deterministic fixtures and certification verdicts; TLC supplies integration execution, application assertions, logs and defect fixes. Establish delivery dates with TBO rather than assuming public documentation turnaround estimates.

plan_context.section: 8. Suggested covering request and support format
paragraphs: Subject: TLC VACATIONS LLP — Flight & Hotel staging scenarios and request/response fixture request

Dear TBO Integration Team, please review the attached scenario plan and tracker. We request account-specific schemas, seeded staging inputs and request/response examples for the supported cases, including negative and recovery cases. Please first confirm the flight mandatory checklist and hotel API family noted in Q01–Q03, and the HotelAPI entitlement noted in Q04. Our client journey uses shortlisted options and a consultant-prepared quote; supplier commitment remains controlled. Please return supported/conditional/unsupported status and proposed fixture delivery dates. Regards, TLC VACATIONS LLP.

For an individual issue, use: environment; agency/API login identifier (no password); scenario/run ID; method/API version; timestamp with timezone; trace/session/request ID; exact error; expected versus actual; reproducibility steps; business impact; and attached casewise JSON logs. Confirm the recipient address with TBO before sending. This covering text is a draft; nothing has been emailed.

Public documentation checked on 17 October 2026. Sections A–C are the onboarding sample and published certification crosswalk; sections D–H are TLC-proposed acceptance and fixture requests, not additional TBO-mandated certification cases. Exact schemas, flags, limits and error codes must be confirmed for the entitled API version. See S8–S11 for method-level contracts supporting the requested field mappings.

Additional input: TBO onboarding email supplied by TLC, and TLC’s local integration verification record dated 6 October 2026. No separate attachment was available; attached-only requirements must be reconciled before final execution.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: API login is separate from portal login; no credentials exposed in UI/log export.

scenarios.group: D. Access and common API contracts

scenarios.execution_steps: One controlled authentication attempt per variant.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Exact HTTP/application error, error message and retry guidance.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Expired-session response and supported recovery chain.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No silent reuse of expired selection; uncertain booking reconciled before retry.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Accepted age classification or documented rejection; airline-specific rule.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No underpriced or invalid passenger category; request clarification if unsupported.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Reconcile new totals and obtain review before any issue call.

scenarios.title: Sold out or stale result index

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Availability/expiry error and whether new search is required.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Worked per-type FareBreakdown mapping and authoritative rounding rules.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Use each type’s passenger count; summed passenger totals reconcile, never average all types.

scenarios.title: GST/business traveller details

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Mandatory/optional status, field validation and retrieval/invoice representation.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Collect required details only; no false confirmation after rejection.

scenarios.title: No SSR and unavailable SSR

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Accepted omission shape and unavailable/stale ancillary errors.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No blank placeholder nodes or unapproved substitution/charge.

scenarios.title: GDS SSR request versus confirmation

scenarios.execution_steps: G with supported SSR fields; retrieve final status.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Request/confirmation status and unsupported options.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Do not label a requested service confirmed unless supplier confirms it.

scenarios.title: Domestic return grouping
scenarios.test_data: Two priced directions with independent result indices.
scenarios.execution_steps: Execute R and retrieve each issued record.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Both chains with leg-to-PNR/ticket mapping; separate failure variant.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Totals and state tracked per leg; no fabricated combined PNR.

scenarios.title: Special return result transition

scenarios.execution_steps: Quote paired selection using agreed syntax, then use returned identifier.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Exact input/output result-index transformation and single/combined booking structure.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Preserve linkage and total; never mix ordinary-return and special-return flows.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: PNR, unticketed state, deadline, release/retry procedure and financial effect.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Record reserved/unticketed, not ticketed; consultant sees recovery action.

scenarios.title: Ticket response times out

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Both final states and lookup by known identifiers/client reference.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No blind duplicate issue; unknown state retained until authoritative resolution.

scenarios.title: Repeated/concurrent submission

scenarios.execution_steps: LOCAL lock test plus TBO-approved duplicate request fixture.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Duplicate handling, supported idempotency/reference scope and lookup path.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: One logical booking/charge; unsupported supplier dedupe covered by TLC locking.

scenarios.title: Only one return leg issues
scenarios.test_data: Outbound confirmed; inbound sold out/issue failure.
scenarios.execution_steps: Two-direction flow with controlled second-leg failure.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Separate final statuses, costs and permitted release/cancel options.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Show partial fulfilment; never announce complete trip or auto-cancel without approval.

scenarios.title: Full and partial cancellation
scenarios.test_data: Ticketed group; whole booking, one passenger and one segment variants.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Eligibility, penalty, request ID, pending/final state and refund amounts if supported.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Unaffected travellers/legs preserved; cancellation request is not refund completion.

scenarios.title: Reissue, schedule change and no-show
scenarios.test_data: Date change; airline cancellation; no-show after departure.
scenarios.execution_steps: Use enabled amendment/status methods or documented manual handoff.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Fare difference/penalty, updated itinerary and unsupported/change-pending cases.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Re-quote and approve costs; retain old/new ticket linkage; route unsupported changes to staff.

scenarios.title: Refund settlement lifecycle
scenarios.test_data: Cancelled ticket with requested, approved, rejected and settled refund states.
scenarios.execution_steps: Poll/status or account reconciliation as TBO supports.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Authoritative state, net refund, deductions and settlement reference.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Bank-credit claims require actual settlement evidence; ledger cannot double-count.

scenarios.title: Booking retrieval consistency
scenarios.test_data: Valid PNR/ID; invalid ID; delayed retrieval; changed status.
scenarios.execution_steps: GetBookingDetails across fixtures.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Full itinerary, traveller/ticket map, state changes and not-found response.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Latest valid supplier state wins; no cross-customer disclosure.

scenarios.title: Branded/corporate fares and fare upsell
scenarios.test_data: Same itinerary with two fare brands or private/corporate fare.
scenarios.execution_steps: Enabled search/upsell path; quote selected brand.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Brand inclusions, eligibility, price and entitlement rejection.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Never merge fares with different baggage/refund conditions or expose private fares publicly.

scenarios.title: City and hotel identifier mapping
scenarios.test_data: New city ID and hotel codes from current static feed; retired ID variant.
scenarios.execution_steps: Resolve city → properties → search.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Current mappings and invalid/retired code response.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No airport-code/city-ID confusion; retired property cannot silently map to another hotel.

scenarios.title: Room combinations remain intact
scenarios.test_data: Two rooms, different adults/children and room types.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Combination code, ordered room/guest mapping and per-room/whole-unit prices.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Do not split or recombine rates from unrelated booking codes.

scenarios.title: Child ages and occupancy limits
scenarios.test_data: Missing age, age-count mismatch, extra child, infant, no adult; positive control.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Allowed ranges and supplier-specific occupancy/extra-bed conditions.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Exact age at check-in preserved; no assumed free infant or guaranteed extra bed.

scenarios.title: Stay/date boundaries
scenarios.test_data: Checkout same/before check-in, past stay, minimum stay, maximum stay, leap-day boundary.
scenarios.execution_steps: Separate Search/PreBook variants.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Validation errors and supported date/stay limits.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Nights calculated correctly; invalid stay cannot be booked.

scenarios.title: Nationality/residency restrictions

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Applicable rate/eligibility and mismatch rejection.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Nationality not changed to obtain a cheaper rate; constraints visible to consultant.

scenarios.title: Room-only versus meal plans
scenarios.test_data: Same hotel with room-only, breakfast and all-inclusive options.
scenarios.execution_steps: Search/PreBook each distinct rate.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Exact meal inclusion, guest coverage and rate identifiers.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Do not assume breakfast covers every guest or all-inclusive includes all extras.

scenarios.title: Refundability and deadline boundary
scenarios.test_data: Refundable/non-refundable; cancellation one minute before/after deadline.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Policy ladder, timezone, indexed room scope, fixed/percent/night rules.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Correct policy presented for selected rate; no inferred timezone or free cancellation.

scenarios.title: Price changes at PreBook
scenarios.test_data: Higher/lower total, changed tax or supplement since Search.
scenarios.execution_steps: Search → PreBook → review.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Updated cost/currency and whether new booking code is returned/required.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Reconcile final amount; require review before Book.

scenarios.title: Policy changes without price change
scenarios.test_data: Same total; refundable becomes restricted or meal inclusion changes.
scenarios.execution_steps: Search then changed PreBook fixture.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Changed policy/inclusions and validity metadata.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Terms change triggers review even when total is unchanged.

scenarios.title: Selected room no longer available

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Sold-out/expired code and permitted re-search path.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No different hotel/room substituted automatically; no false confirmation.

scenarios.title: Taxes, supplements and currency

scenarios.execution_steps: Search → PreBook → confirmed retrieval.
scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Charge scope, currency, inclusion flags, nightly/total values and settlement amount.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No double-counted tax; payable-now and payable-at-property clearly separated.

scenarios.title: Minimum selling restriction

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Restriction applicability and authoritative currency/amount semantics.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Applicable floor enforced; never convert or omit it without an agreed rule. [S6]

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No package-only rate sold standalone; transfers not promised from hotel description alone.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No blind duplicate reservation; unresolved stays unknown.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Voucher availability, confirmation/reference fields and premature-request error.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Policy outcome, penalty, approved/refused refund and settlement evidence.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No promised refund without supplier outcome; avoid duplicate financial posting.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Not-found versus pending versus final failure; updated booking details.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Do not mark cancelled from transient not-found; escalate unresolved mismatch.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Fallback is honest; no fabricated star rating, accessibility or distance.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Expiry semantics and stale-selection response.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Only authorised data exported; no tokens, passports or volatile rates treated as durable facts.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Ignore safe additions; unknown critical values fail visibly, not silently misclassified.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No wrong-hotel image/description attached to a bookable option.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Coherent search/quote fixtures; no new package API assumed.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Selections remain alternatives; supplier booking is not called by shortlist submission.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Clear per-party/per-room units and currencies for each fixture.

scenarios.requested_tbo_fixture: Amenity/inclusion evidence and unavailable/missing-value variants.
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: No unsupported preference guarantees; recommendations link back to current supplier evidence.
